_README: Per-network indexing metadata. THE ONLY hand-maintained file in the subgraph
toolchain. Everything else is generated from this plus build/deployments.json:
networks.json    address + startBlock per network   (graph-cli reads it)
graph-node.toml  chain sections for self-hosted     (graph-node reads it)
regenerate both:  npm run networks
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL
The first cut of this toolchain hardcoded testnet names into npm script names
(build:0g-testnet, deploy:monad-testnet, ...) and into two hand-written chain
sections in graph-node.toml. That meant broadcasting a mainnet factory would
have required renaming scripts and hand-editing TOML -- exactly the kind of
work that gets skipped, leaving a stack that says testnet while indexing
mainnet. Mainnet entries are already here, complete, waiting for an address.
target = studio       deployed to Subgraph Studio, no infrastructure of ours
target = self-hosted  deployed to our own Graph Node (subgraph/docker-compose.yml)
`target` is not a preference. It is what The Graph does and does not serve,
checked against graphprotocol/networks-registry v0.7.111. A network with no
Subgraphs support cannot go to Studio no matter how much we would like it to.
maxBlockRange is the eth_getLogs ceiling the RPC actually enforces, probed
directly rather than assumed -- see the `probed` field on each entry. Set it
too high and every request fails; too low and a backfill takes days.
Only meaningful for self-hosted networks; Studio runs its own providers.

0g.label: 0G Mainnet
0g.probed: 2026-08-18 Geth/v1.15.11: eth_getLogs 10000-block span OK, genesis header OK, eth_getBlockReceipts OK, trace_block and debug_traceBlockByNumber both -32601. Pruned, not archive: eth_getBalance on old blocks fails with 'missing trie node'. Range held at 2000 because the 10000 ceiling is a log-count limit, not a block limit, and a busy contract would blow past it.

0g-testnet.probed: 2026-08-18 Geth/v1.15.11, chainId 0x40da: eth_getLogs 10000-block span OK, genesis header OK, eth_getBlockReceipts OK, no traces.

monad.label: Monad Mainnet
monad.probed: 2026-08-18 Monad/0.15.1, chainId 0x8f: eth_getLogs HARD CAP at 100 blocks -- HTTP 413 with {"code":-32614,"message":"eth_getLogs is limited to a 100 range"} for 500 and above. genesis header OK, eth_getBlockReceipts OK, trace_block -32601 (debug_traceBlockByNumber does answer, unused). A paid provider lifts the 100 cap; raise maxBlockRange only after re-probing.
monad.registry: listed, but Subgraphs not served (Firehose and Substreams only)

monad-testnet.probed: 2026-08-18 Monad/0.16.0, chainId 0x279f: same 100-block eth_getLogs cap as mainnet. genesis header OK, eth_getBlockReceipts OK.
monad-testnet.registry: listed, no Graph services at all

devchain.label: Local Hardhat devchain
devchain.probed: not probed; local node, no limits
devchain.note: Named `devchain`, NOT `mainnet`. The usual hardhat-with-graph-node convention is to call chainId 31337 `mainnet`, which then shows up as the network on every local deployment and in every status query. graph-node does not require that name -- it only requires the manifest and this config to agree.
